source.check: deemed re-elected: no nomination for the division, whose sitting member was returned (Belfast News-Letter, 1936-05-08, p. 3); sat as a member at the meeting reported in the Lisburn Standard, 1936-07-17, p. 8 (monthly meeting, Wednesday 15 July 1936) (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on 7 May 1936. One new member, Mr. William Porter, was returned for Ballykeel; in the other nine divisions (Ballymacbrennan, Ballyskeagh, Blaris, Breda, Carryduff, Dromara, Drumbo, Edenderry, Hillsborough) the sitting members were automatically returned, five of whom are recorded from Lisburn Standard reports of the June and July 1936 meetings (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). Polling in County Down was fixed for 28 May 1936. One place-name in the list is John Martin's address, not a division; he is the member for Anahilt. Filed on 1936-06-04, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Down that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1936-05-28 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Ballyskeagh (A. A. Gillespie, co-opted for it in March 1931) is added from the meeting of 9 June 1936 (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 1930 return (Robert J. M'Cormack, Drumbo, from the meetings pass); the Lisburn Standard report names the member as sitting within six months of 4 June 1936. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
